copy.blurb:
England face Croatia on Wednesday, evening UTC kickoff, in FIFA World Cup 2026. This is one of the matches where the model's number disagrees with the closing line on Polymarket — a substantive gap on the Croatia side, +7.7pp.

Elo numbers going in: England 1950, Croatia 1860. That's a 90-point lead for England — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: England to win at 47%, the draw at 25%, and Croatia to win at 28%. The Desk's three-way distribution is calibrated against the W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on, not against the exact scoreline. Croatia sits at 28% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: England to win at 56%, the draw at 25%, and Croatia to win at 20%. Polymarket has Croatia at 20%, which prices out at American odds of +388; the model has the same side at 28%. The +7.7pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Croatia the lower bound is 24%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +3.3pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures — we're not claiming the market is generally wrong, only that this side, on this fixture, looks mispriced. Selection is the dimension this verdict adds value on.

This number will move. Confirmed starting elevens, injuries, weather at the venue, and suspensions carried in from previous fixtures all re-enter the prior on the late-binding cadence. With kickoff 29 days out, we're still on weekly refresh; the daily cadence picks up inside T-5d. The Pick can flip to a Pass if news moves enough of the prior. The Desk does not tip and does not recommend a trade — the model price, the market price, and the gap across them are what's on the page.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Croatia a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +7.7pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: On Croatia, the model is +7.7pp out from Polymarket. Our number reads 28%; the market reads 20%. That gap is the basis for the Pick.
copy.title: England v Croatia · the model leans Croatia
